key_insight: Denoising diffusion models generate realistic additive-manufacturing microstructure images and enable inverse mappings from properties or process conditions to structure.
engineering_relevance: Synthetic microstructures could support crystal-plasticity simulations and uncertainty quantification to accelerate qualification of additively manufactured metals.
method: Train diffusion models to synthesize digital-twin orientation-imaging micrographs.
Use classifier-free guidance for property-to-structure and process-to-structure inverse mapping.
Demonstrate a qualification-relevant uncertainty quantification application.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports quantitative evidence of generated-sample fidelity but provides no dataset sizes, evaluation metrics, or numerical results.
watch_item: Image fidelity alone does not establish accurate downstream mechanical-property predictions; validation with crystal-plasticity simulations and experiments remains important.
paper_title: Microstructural Generative Inverse Models for Additive Manufacturing Digital Twins
